findings.finding: Broad ordering is consistent: Vance has the clearest organization, Rubio a credible alternative, Cruz a narrower competing lane. DeSantis and McEntee require more coalition-building assumptions.

Faction evidence does not calibrate precise probabilities. The 1.30-point Rubio–DeSantis gap and McEntee’s 3.90 are particularly assumption-sensitive. No exact reallocation is justified by this consistency pass alone.

Corrected the omission of historical immigration-oriented staffing and strengthened executive-control experience. Confirmed withdrawal drafting/signature involvement in the primary committee record. Do not reduce him to a content creator.
Use current faction homes; populist is a dissolved archival faction. Do not invent a unified media/insurgent constituency or automatically assign it to any nominee.
Miller/Wiles transition and Trump endorsement uncertainty affect the channels all contenders must navigate; none is an automatic nomination preference.
No conversion of legacy faction scores to odds; observed support, ideological preference, business investment, paid clients and prospective coalition transfer remain separate.
